securityInterpretation.acceptedContract: A mutable name-ordered browsing session may omit or repeat a membership, but every page and exact lookup recomputes current identity authority; browser merge is ID-deduplicated; search/reload recovers navigation drift.

verificationLimitations: The database mutations are test-harness fixture controls applied between page requests and restored before terminal assertions; they do not exercise the product membership-administration API or its audit workflow.
The browser responses are synthetic same-origin fixtures and do not compose a real identity provider with mutation timing.

The exercise does not prove scaled mutation rates, multiple simultaneous administrators, serializable snapshots, substantially larger directories, representative timing, multi-host behavior, staging, or rolling deployment.

The locally built PostgreSQL distribution does not include the optional amcheck extension; two attempted pg_amcheck invocations correctly reported that no relations could be checked, so no amcheck claim is made.
No credential, token, session cookie, customer data, or production payload is recorded.
